critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
The match plate does its job and is the best-built frame in the stage. It is a level, frontal evidence-display composition: the bench is centred (x 150-1125), the bags sit a touch right of centre, there is a quiet block wall above for the type, and the straight cut registers. Measured on the raw PNGs, phase correlation of gradient maps between match and void_stage bags gives a 0,0 px shift in the suitcase, duffel and handle windows. A 50/50 blend of the frames either side of 2.0 s in match_to_void.mp4 shows no doubling. The bright band under the bags carries across the cut. At x 300 / 595 / 1000 (rows 490-530) the bench top reads about 115 / 165 / 105 graded, and the void pool reads about 88 / 141 / 85 at the same pixels. The pool is the same width as the bench.

The frame fails on one thing a match cut cannot survive: the suitcase changes value. The whole case is about twice as bright as in void_stage bags. Its front pocket grades 77 median (p90 103) against 29 (p90 52), its side panel 36 against 17, the handle bar 100 against 42, and the lid 131 against 65. In the cut itself the pocket averages 77 at 1.90 s and 31 at 2.10 s. The duffel's shadowed front holds (13 against 14). In this stage's own empty, wide and two_shot the case grades 13-14. So on the cut the case reads as a lighter grey bag that turns black. The empty frame (same Ch 11 beat) and match also disagree with each other: in empty the duffel is the grey one (43) and the case the black one (13), and match reverses that. The likely cause is the bench troffer (360 W). It is broad and only about 1.3 m above the case, and in the match layout most of it lies on the camera side of the pocket's plane. The pocket face therefore takes top light at a far less grazing angle than under the void's spot, which hangs almost straight down from 5.8 m. In the ch00/ch11 layout the troffer is behind the pocket, so the case stays black there. The case's base colour is already capped at about 0.05 by FINISH, so this is light, not albedo.

Second, the luggage tag lies flat on the lid as a pale, slightly cool card, about 40x8 px at 1280. It peaks at 230 graded at (518, 272), which ties with the bench's front-edge glint for the brightest value in the frame, right at the registration point. The tag is not in the void plate, so it pops off at the cut.

Smaller faults in the plate:
- Cut fragments at the frame edges read as clutter, not place:
  - the back of the scanner's monitor, a near-black panel with a slightly lighter rim (x 0-75, y 255-480)
  - the conveyor and its tray (bottom-left)
  - the far rim of the under-bench shelf_tray (x 680-965, y 690-720)
- The bumper rail's lower edge runs parallel to the duffel's top within about 5-10 px, a near-tangent.
- The bench top is a plain, even slab with no visible brushing, even when contrast-stretched.
- The plate is 1280x720, but the composite is mastered at 1920 and holds about 10 s under YES.

At the stage level, nothing else has moved. Wide, overhead, tag, two_shot and empty are still the 06:14 regrades of the round-5 renders (1e693ae). handbags.jpg (published in 7018060 at 08:09) predates the code it is published against. Since 0ffcc04, well before 62bdb11, CAMERAS["handbags"] cheats Dawn to (1.75, -1.10) and uses pose bag_insert with OfficerA's hands behind him. The published frame still shows the headless lapelled torso and the hand hovering over the tote. So all of r6's open faults still show: the overhead's white hand, the near-white tag card, the cap fit and the flat scanner. enter and dawn_close are not published for review at all, although SCRIPT_V2 cuts them into the cold open ahead of match (dawn_close directly before it). The scores are unchanged. The match alone lifts composition and story read half a point over round 6, but without the re-renders the rest of the stage stays at its round-6 level. Not pro level yet. The match is two fixes away from being the strongest cut in the film.
answers:
Q1. Do the two silhouettes register against void_stage bags? Yes. I measured on the raw PNGs, not only the blend. Phase correlation of gradient magnitude gives (0, 0) px in all three windows: suitcase (x 400-600, y 200-510), duffel (590-970, 360-540) and handle (440-530, 205-260). The peak correlations are 0.44, 0.55 and 0.54. I also took a 50/50 blend of the frames at 1.90 s and 2.10 s from out/gfx/cut/match_to_void.mp4 (1920x1080). The case outline, handle, wheels, duffel body and both strap loops coincide, with no doubling. Your 0.003 px vertex figure is consistent with that.

What does not register is value and detail:
(a) The suitcase. In match the whole case is about twice as bright as in void bags:
- front pocket: 77 median (p90 103) against 29 (p90 52)
- side panel: 36 against 17
- handle bar: 100 against 42
- lid: 131 against 65
The same pair of video frames confirms it: the pocket averages 77 before the cut and 31 after. The duffel's front holds (13 against 14), but its lit top band (x 640-930, y 380-400) also reads 99 against 63. The case grades 13-14 in this stage's empty, wide and two_shot, so match is the outlier. On the cut, the case reads as a lighter grey bag going black, which undercuts "the same bags".
(b) The tag. It is a pale, slightly cool card lying on the lid, about 40x8 px at 1280 (x 490-530, y 265-273). It peaks at 230 graded at (518, 272), tied with the bench's front-edge glint for the frame's brightest value. It is in match and not in void, so it blinks out at the exact point where the eye is registering the bags.
(c) The zip pulls hang differently: short pale tabs in match, long dark pulls in void. This is minor.

Q2. Is the wall quiet enough for the later YES composite while the room still reads?

Quiet: yes, with margin, and close to your numbers. The graded title box (x 420-860, y 30-200) reads median 39, p90 45, peak 50. The local high-pass (luminance minus a 5 px blur) peaks at about -5 / +5 levels, with 98% of pixels within -3 / +2. The mortar coursing never competes with the cream YES at about 232. In match_yes.png the word reads cleanly with nothing letter-like behind it. Do not darken the wall further. Its vertical profile is right as it stands:
- about 23 at the top edge
- rising from about 33 to 46 down the title box (y 30-200)
- 46-48 behind the bags (y 255-345)
That gives the bags a soft halo and the type a slightly darker field.

Does the room read? As an institutional room, yes: block coursing, the two-tone wall split at the bumper rail, chrome bench legs, the wall/floor junction and floor tiles. As an inspection room, only through what comes before it. The cut fragments at the edges (the monitor's back, the conveyor, the under-bench tray) are too small and too dark to say "scanner", and they read as clutter. That is acceptable, because the cold open reaches match through two_shot and dawn_close, and chapter 4 through enter and wide. Tidy the fragments rather than add identifiers.

For the composite (the lead's lane): the bottom of YES sits about 25 px (at 720; 38 px at 1080) above the top of the case's handle. That is tight but workable.

Q3 (the job and the cut). The straight cut is what the film's rule asks for: YES holds, with no dissolve and no black. The wall drops out, the bench becomes the pool at the same width and nearly the same brightness, and the meaning lands: the same bags, now in the void. The cut would be seamless if the suitcase were brought down to the void plate's value (pocket about 30 graded) and the tag were taken off for this camera. As published, a viewer at 1080 will notice two things: the case's jump in value and the vanishing tag.

fixes.problem: The suitcase is lit about twice as bright as in void_stage bags, all over. Front pocket: 77 median (p90 103) against 29 (p90 52). Side panel: 36 against 17. Handle bar: 100 against 42. Lid: 131 against 65. In match_to_void.mp4 the pocket averages 77 at 1.90 s and 31 at 2.10 s. The duffel's shadowed front holds (13 against 14), but its lit top band (x 640-930, y 380-400) reads 99 against 63. The likely cause is the bench troffer (360 W, about 1.3 m above the case). In this layout (case at (0.32, -0.10), turned 122 degrees) most of it sits on the camera side of the pocket's plane, so the face takes top light at a much less grazing angle than under the void's spot, which hangs almost straight down from 5.8 m. In the ch00/ch11 layout the troffer is behind the pocket, which is why empty, wide and two_shot hold the case at 13-14. troffer_scanner_light cannot reach the case directly: it points straight down with an 80-degree spread, and the case is about 55 degrees off its axis. mon_spill (9 W) is aimed at the case's front from about 1.9 m, but it cannot explain the lid and handle. The base colour is already capped at about 0.05 by FINISH's ceiling, so this is light, not albedo.
fixes.fix:
The camera and layout are locked for registration, so lower the case's value for this camera only. In apply_camera(), after set_beat(), when name == "match", scale the case's materials and restore them for every other camera. Use either the HueSaturation node's Value (now 0.9) or a multiply after the ceiling Darken. Start at 0.4 and step down. The view transform and the grade are non-linear, so the factor that brings 77 to about 30 may be well below 0.4. A shadow-only flag over the camera side of the case is an alternative, in the manner of 'match wall cutter', if the lead prefers to leave the material untouched. In the same test, also hide mon_spill for match: it is cheap and off-frame. Leave troffer_scanner_light alone, as it is not the cause. Re-render match with --nocast at 1280x720 and measure:
- the pocket (x 470-580, y 320-440) at 25-40 graded median, with p90 at most 55
- the handle bar (x 455-515, y 214-222) and the lid (x 450-580, y 270-300) near the void's 42 and 65
- the side panel (x 425-465) at least 8 levels below the wall behind it (x 360-412, now 32)
- the handle and the lid edge still carrying a top-light rim
If the duffel's lit top band still reads well above the void's 63, give it the same treatment, more gently. Then re-run the 50/50 blend against void bags: the case should differ by no more than about 10 graded levels.

fixes.problem: The luggage tag lies flat on the lid as a pale, slightly cool card (about 209, 210, 213 graded), about 40x8 px at x 490-530, y 265-273. It peaks at 230 graded at (518, 272), which ties with the bench's front-edge glint for the brightest value in the frame, right at the registration point. It is not in void_stage bags, so it pops off on the cut.
fixes.fix:
Hide it for this camera only. The tag, its ring and its twine (luggage_tag, luggage_tag_ring, luggage_tag_twine) are parented to the case, so set_beat() shows them again with the case in every layout that has it. In apply_camera(), after set_beat(), add a plain block: if name == "match", loop over _STATE["props"]["dawn-suitcase"].children_recursive and set hide_render = True on every object whose name starts with "luggage_tag". Do not set hide_render = (name == "match") for every camera: the 'three bags' layout hides the case, and that line would un-hide the tag in mid-air.
Check: no pixel above about 180 in x 486-532, y 262-278 (now 230). The case-top window (x 440-600, y 250-300) will still read p99 about 176 from the over-lit lid until fix 1 brings it toward the void's 116.
Trade-off: the tag shows on the handle in wide, about 6-13 s earlier in the cold open. At this size its absence will not be noticed, and the cut gains more than it loses. If the lead would rather keep the tag across the cut, it has to be added to void_stage at a matched value (and toned to buff, as r6 asked). That is not this stage's file, so flag it in the reply.

fixes.camera: handbags, overhead, wide, two_shot, tag, empty (and the unpublished enter, dawn_close)
fixes.problem: The stage's published frames are stale against the code at 62bdb11. handbags.jpg (published in 7018060 at 08:09) still shows the headless lapelled torso and OfficerA's hand hovering over the tote. Since 0ffcc04 (09:24), CAMERAS['handbags'] has cheated Dawn to (1.75, -1.10), and pose bag_insert puts OfficerA's hands behind him. The other five frames are the 06:14 regrades of the round-5 renders (1e693ae), so they still show the white hand in the overhead, the near-white tag card, the caps and the flat scanner. SCRIPT_V2 cuts enter (0:20) and dawn_close (0:27, directly before match) into the cold open, but neither is in frames/graded/inspection_room/.
fixes.fix:
Re-render and publish handbags, overhead, wide, two_shot, tag and empty, plus enter and dawn_close, with shoot.py at --res 1280x720 --spp 64, then run regrade_frames.sh. Then run r6's checks on the new frames:
- no figure crosses the handbags frame's top edge, and no hand hovers above the tote
- the near bench top in handbags reads about 45-65 graded
- the cap bands sit on the head all round
- the duffel's opening reads darker than its outside
- the tag card grades buff, with R clearly above B
- the scanner's right side reads above 10 graded
Without these frames the rest of the stage cannot move past its round-6 level, however good the match is.

fixes.problem: The plate is 1280x720, but the composite (match_yes.png) and the cut (match_to_void.mp4) are mastered at 1920x1080. This frame holds about 10 s under YES in the cold open (0:33-0:43) and is the film's last cut, so a 1.5x upscale softens the case's zips and the duffel's folds exactly where the eye rests.
fixes.fix: Render match at --res 1920x1080 --spp 64, and ask void_stage for bags at 1920x1080 too (its raw is also 1280x720). The cameras keep the same 36 mm sensor and lens and the same 16:9 aspect, so the registration holds. Before the lead re-composites, repeat the gradient phase correlation at 1920 to verify it (expect a 0,0 shift).

fixes.problem:
Cut fragments at the frame edges read as clutter, not place.
(1) The back of the scanner's monitor (mon_body; by projection x -195 to 60, y 257-485) shows at x 0-75, y 255-480 as a near-black panel (median 5) with a slightly lighter rim (about 20-25) against the wall's 16. It reads like a doorway.
(2) A dark tray edge sits at the bottom centre (x 680-965, y 690-720), cut by the frame's bottom edge. By projection it is the far rim of the under-bench shelf_tray: a 0.6 x 0.4 m tray turned 2 degrees, at (-0.42, 0.02, 0.27), whose rim falls at about y 694. The bench shelf's own edges project below the frame.
(3) The conveyor and its tray sit in the bottom-left corner.
fixes.fix: Do not reframe: the camera is locked for registration. For match only, in apply_camera(), set hide_render = (name == "match") on shelf_tray and on the monitor's parts (mon_body, mon_screen, mon_vesa, mon_arm, mon_pivot, mon_wallplate). Nothing else toggles these objects, so the other cameras are unaffected. Keep the conveyor at the bottom-left: it is dark (median 15) and gives depth. Checks: x 0-75, y 255-480 reads as the adjacent wall (about 16 median, nothing above about 25), and the bottom rows between the bench legs (x 680-965, y 690-720) read as floor, with no straight dark edge across them.

fixes.problem: The front wall's bumper rail (rail_f, z 0.96-1.07, with the dado paint split at its top) projects to y 359-391. Its lower edge runs parallel to the duffel's top (y about 380-396) within about 5-10 px for most of the bag's length. This near-tangent flattens the bag's top line during the 10 s hold under YES. The outline itself still holds (the lit top reads about 99 against 36 for the rail between the bags), so this is a minor composition point.
fixes.fix: For match only, lower rail_f by about 0.25 m (to about z 0.70-0.81). Move the block wall's dado split to 0.81 as well: it is the LESS_THAN node fed by split_z 1.07 in the 'block wall' material. Toggle both in apply_camera() and restore them for every other camera; handbags, for one, sees the front wall. The rail and split then project to about y 434-465, behind the bags' bodies. Leave cove_f alone: it is the floor-level cove and plays no part in this. Check that no horizontal line runs within 10 px of the duffel's top edge.
